name: Dawning Isles
summary: The Dawning Isles lie blighted beneath the Vile Fin murlocs’ growing numbers. Along Silverpine Forest’s eastern edge, the islets rise from Lordamere Lake, where the Plague of Undeath has left their shores rotting.

sections.title: Blight on the Lake
sections.body: The Dawning Isles lie under the Vile Fin murlocs’ claim. Before the Third War, these keys rested amid Lordamere Lake’s calm, clear waters. When the Plague of Undeath swept across Lordaeron, corruption spread through the shallows. The vegetation turned pallid and rotting, and the islands lost their former peace. Now the Vile Fin murlocs hold the muddy shores and tangled brush. They defend their growing colonies against anyone who tries to cross the lake.

sections.title: A Murloc Stronghold
sections.body: Bog beasts once prowled the blighted Dawning Isles alongside the murlocs. The bog beasts have since vanished, leaving the Vile Fin population to swell. The murlocs now control the isles outright, making the chain of keys their stronghold on Lordamere Lake.

faq.q: Where are the Dawning Isles located?
faq.answer: The Dawning Isles rise from Lordamere Lake along Silverpine Forest’s eastern boundary, just west of the Ruins of Lordaeron.

faq.q: What creatures inhabit the Dawning Isles?
faq.answer: The Vile Fin tribe of murlocs thrives along the corrupted shores. Bog beasts once prowled the islets too, but they have since largely vanished as the murloc population has grown.

faq.q: Why are the trees and shores rotting here?
faq.answer: The Plague of Undeath tainted the Dawning Isles when it swept across Lordaeron during the Third War. The water and soil absorbed the blight, poisoning the vegetation and leaving the islets murky, sickly, and decayed.

angles.text: The blighted Dawning Isles lie on Lordamere Lake, within sight of the Undercity’s western approaches. The Vile Fin murlocs that hold them grow more numerous each year.
The blighted Dawning Isles show how far the Scourge’s corruption reached into Lordaeron’s scenic waters.
